### Welcome!

Hello and welcome to my page! My name is Adrianna Martinez and I am a first-generation student pursuing a Master's degree in Geosciences at the Jackson School of Geosciences, University of Texas at Austin.  I work under the advisement of Dr. Brent Elliott and serve as a Graduate Research Assistant at the Bureau of Economic Geology, where I study rare earth element (REE) transport mechanisms in the laccoliths of West Texas, focusing on the Sierra Blanca Complex.

I completed my Bachelor's of Science in Environmental Studies with a minor in Earth Science at UC Santa Barbara, where the landscape itself made the case for geology daily; mountains rising transversely, active faults, and rapidly eroding marine terraces compressing so many processes into a single place. Through coursework in GIS, energy policy, and soil science, I found myself continually pulled toward the geological controls beneath the environmental systems I was studying. That pull, combined with a growing awareness of the mineral demands of the clean energy transition, led me toward critical mineral systems and eventually to studying how hydrothermal fluids mobilize and concentrate REEs.

Outside of academics, I enjoy off-roading, skiing, tennis, drawing and painting, camping, and running, as well as exploring new landscapes and their geologic stories.

My current research examines whether the vapor-phase crystallization process responsible for REE-fluoride mineralization at Round Top — one of the few recognized HREE resource prospects for US critical mineral production — extends across the broader five-laccolith complex or is unique to Round Top itself. You can learn more about this project on my [research page](projects.qmd).
